- Overestimate prices when sentiment is positive (especially >0.11) — model tends to overshoot in bullish periods.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is negative (especially < -0.3) — model fails to capture downside risk or mean reversion.
- Model exhibits lagged response: true price drops often occur after model peaks, especially after sentiment spikes.
- After a sharp price spike, model overcorrects downward — forecast dips too early or too steeply.
- Mean reversion bias: model holds prices too high for extended periods after recent highs, ignoring recent sentiment decay.
- Forecast horizon 30d: model consistently overestimates early in the window (first 5–7 days) and underestimates late (last 5–7 days) — adjust for asymmetric decay.
- Sentiment-driven volatility: when sentiment is volatile (e.g., alternating +0.11 and -0.3), model fails to smooth transitions — forecast jumps too abruptly.
